clue.text: Understudy's name suddenly in lights and fortunately twinkling

definitions.meaning: an understudy who gets a big break by chance becomes a fortunate headline performer
a heavenly body shining kindly on someone, bringing good fortune

explanation.walkthrough: Both halves describe the same two-word phrase: one as a stage break-through, one as a benign heavenly body.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer thrust into fame by fortune, and a twinkling celestial body that brings good luck, both carry this phrase.

clue.text: Gone down in naval history

parts.note: reads as being remembered by historians of the navy, but describes a vessel or sailor that has sunk and vanished on the ocean

explanation.definitionFit: Ships that sink and are never recovered are recorded as missing on the ocean, the fate of many a warship.

clue.text: Oriental characters put down like this

definitions.meaning: from the Far East, here the most populous Asian nation
a style of writing in logographic characters, as in Mandarin script

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective names someone from the People's Republic and also the script whose ideograms are written in that language.

clue.text: Christmas records may make the sparks fly

parts.note: Yule is the old name for the festive season in December
logs are written records, as in a ship's log

explanation.surface: Seasonal records might provoke heated arguments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make the sparks fly' suggests a row; it is the literal crackle of big pieces of wood burning on the hearth at the festive season.
explanation.definitionFit: Large festive pieces of timber burnt in the fireplace throw out sparks as they burn.

clue.text: Have a brush with it after awkward meal in a sitting position

indicators.note: the shuffled letters of meal are placed inside the word for a seat

parts.note: a chair is a seat, a place where one sits

indicators.note: awkward suggests the letters of meal are arranged clumsily into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice to have a quarrel after an uncomfortable dinner eaten while seated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkward' scrambles the meal, and 'in' sets the result inside the seat. 'Have a brush with it' sounds like a squabble, but means a paintbrush made of this soft fibre.
explanation.definitionFit: Artists' soft brushes are traditionally made from the fine fur of a desert animal (in practice often squirrel).

clue.text: Petticoat management that sounds bad as a rule

indicators.note: signals that the phrase for petticoat management is said aloud to give a word spelt differently

parts.note: petticoat government is rule by women, so a female ruler's administration is a 'Miss government'

explanation.surface: Being ruled by women is said to be a poor form of government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Petticoat government' is an old phrase for women in charge; 'Miss government' heard aloud is the word for bad rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Poor or incompetent administration of a state is bad rule.

clue.text: See 3
High-powered traveller coming round by way of a hill

indicators.note: the words for a hill come round the word for by way of, enclosing it

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor
via means by way of

explanation.surface: A powerful traveller passes over a hill on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming round' has the hill enclose the 'by way of' word. A tor is a craggy hilltop, typical of Dartmoor in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot travels high in the air in an engine-powered machine.

clue.text: … calling for a man who has got the message

definitions.text: … calling for a man who has got the message

parts.words: calling for a man who has got the message
parts.note: both a man's name one might call out and the radio word said by someone confirming a transmission received

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis ties it to the previous clue only on the page. In radio procedure the word means 'message received', and it is also a man's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio operators reply with this word to acknowledge receipt, and it is a common male forename.

clue.text: Upset, sick at heart, rushed round

indicators.note: the word for sick sits at the heart, the middle, of the other word
the word for rushed goes round the word for sick

parts.note: sped means rushed
ill means sick

explanation.surface: Feeling queasy and having hurried about, someone is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: ILL in the middle of SPED: SP(ILL)ED. 'Upset' looks like an emotional state but means knocked over, as with milk.
explanation.definitionFit: Knocked over, as a drink tipped from a cup.

clue.text: At least the hanger-on has one reliable quality

definitions.text: At least the hanger-on has one reliable quality

parts.words: At least the hanger-on has one reliable quality
parts.note: a hanger-on depends on others, so the one trait such a person surely has is the ability to depend, which is also the word for trustworthiness

explanation.definitionFit: Trustworthiness is the quality of being reliable; split up the word reads 'depend' plus 'ability', the hanger-on's skill.

clue.text: Drunken Pygmalion professor sounding weary

indicators.note: drunken suggests the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: Professor Henry Higgins is the phonetics teacher in Shaw's play Pygmalion

explanation.surface: The professor from Shaw's play, tipsy, sounds tired.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram is of HIGGINS, not of the printed words. 'Sounding weary' is the definition, describing someone breathing out heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: Letting out long, audible breaths is what a tired or sad person does.

clue.text: Primate cross, it sounds like pique

parts.note: an ape is a primate
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: A monkey crosses itself and gets in a huff.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is indirect: 'pique' is pronounced like 'peak', and a peak is the top point, which is what this word means.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest point of something is its peak, a word pronounced the same as pique.

clue.text: Sulphur on water giving angler the wind up

parts.note: S is the chemical symbol for sulphur
a pool is a body of water

explanation.surface: A whiff of sulphur on the pond frightens a fisherman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The wind up' looks like fright; it is the literal winding-up of fishing line, done on a reel. 'on' places S before POOL in a down-style charade.
explanation.definitionFit: A reel or bobbin around which a fisherman's line is wound.

clue.text: See 1
Arms order that's not on the level

definitions.meaning: a drill command to rest a rifle on the shoulder
ground that is inclined rather than flat

explanation.definitionFit: The drill command to shoulder rifles, and an incline or gradient that is not flat.

clue.text: Fifth grade can set one's teeth on edge

definitions.text: can set one's teeth on edge

parts.note: G is the fifth note of the scale of C major (C, D, E, F, G)
rate means grade, as in first-rate

explanation.surface: A child in the fifth year of school can be very annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fifth grade' reads as an American school year, but splits into G (the fifth note up from C) and RATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To grate is to irritate, like a harsh scraping noise.

clue.text: Putting a curse on the wrong purson?

definitions.text: Putting a curse on the wrong purson?

parts.words: Putting a curse on the wrong purson?
parts.note: reads as a witch's misdirected hex, but casting a spell is 'spelling', and 'purson' is a misspelt word

explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'purson' is a deliberate misspelling, which is the point of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistake in how a word is written, such as 'purson' for 'person'.

clue.text: He acts a bonny prince

definitions.meaning: someone who makes believe or feigns
Bonnie Prince Charlie, the Young claimant to the British throne in 1745

explanation.definitionFit: One who feigns, and a claimant to a throne, as Charles Edward Stuart, called the Young claimant, was.

clue.text: Head firm where the privileged sit on board

definitions.text: where the privileged sit on board

parts.note: a captain is a head or leader
stable means firm

explanation.surface: The company boss's seat is reserved for the elite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' means on a ship: favoured passengers dine with the ship's commander.
explanation.definitionFit: On a cruise ship, honoured passengers are invited to dine with the master of the vessel.

clue.text: Big fiddler living like a hermit?

definitions.text: Big fiddler living like a hermit?

parts.words: Big fiddler living like a hermit?
parts.note: a player of a large string instrument, and, split up, one who lives in a monk's small room

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who plays the large bowed instrument held between the knees; a hermit lives in a cell.

clue.text: Hold up of potted lobster

indicators.note: potted, like food preserved in a jar, suggests the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A delay caused by a jar of preserved shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold up' looks like a delay but is a verb meaning support.
explanation.definitionFit: To support or prop up, as a cushion props a sleeper.

clue.text: Daring verses and sketches not lightly committed to paper

definitions.text: sketches not lightly committed to paper
definitions.meaning: drawing strokes made heavily and thickly rather than faintly

explanation.definitionFit: Audacious lines of poetry, and heavy, thick strokes of a pen or pencil.

clue.text: Bar one little woman for constantly strumming fingers

parts.note: to bar is to ban
Jo March is one of the sisters in Louisa May Alcott's Little Women

explanation.surface: Prohibit a girl who keeps drumming her fingers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strumming fingers' sounds like a nervous habit; it is a string instrument always plucked by fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: A round-bodied string instrument played by strumming, as in bluegrass music.

clue.text: See 21
A draught for smokers

parts.note: reads as a cold breeze for cigarette users, but means the duct that draws air up through a fire or chimney

explanation.definitionFit: A chimney duct carries smoke away from fires and stoves, and creates a draught.

clue.text: Dirty blow for the man at the wheel

definitions.meaning: an illegal punch in boxing, or a nasty gust

definitions.text: for the man at the wheel
definitions.meaning: for a helmsman, an adverse breeze that blows against his course

explanation.definitionFit: An unfair blow, and an adverse gale that troubles a helmsman steering his ship.

clue.text: See 24
Half nobility nursing air of importance in E. Africa

indicators.note: the first half of nobility holds, as if nursing, the word for an air of importance
half signals taking the first four of the eight letters of nobility

parts.note: an air is a manner or bearing, as in putting on airs

explanation.surface: Half the aristocracy put on grand airs in East Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: NOBI is the first half of NOBILITY; it holds AIR: N(AIR)OBI. The definition is just 'in E. Africa', the capital's location.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Kenya is a city located in East Africa.

clue.text: Spun yarn

parts.note: thread that has been twirled, and also a story given a deceitful spin

explanation.definitionFit: Spun thread is twirled, and a 'spun yarn' is a story told with a deceptive turn.

clue.text: Skilfully beaten, and not only at indoor games

definitions.text: Skilfully beaten, and not only at indoor games

parts.words: Skilfully beaten, and not only at indoor games
parts.note: defeated by greater skill, and, split up, playing outside rather than indoors

explanation.definitionFit: Being outclassed by a more skilful opponent; split up it suggests playing out of doors.

clue.text: Ruder management engraved in Germany's past

indicators.note: management suggests the letters of ruder are handled into a new order

explanation.surface: Coarser administration was carved into German history.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to Albrecht Dürer, the German Renaissance artist famed for his engravings.
explanation.definitionFit: Albrecht Dürer was a sixteenth-century German master printmaker who engraved copper plates.
